chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated that his father narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim and others, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that he said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade a man from answering anyone or speaking to him while he is relieving himself, until he has finished.

key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: The toilet or place of relieving oneself
key_terms.يَفْرَغَ: To finish or complete the act

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette for answering calls or speaking while relieving oneself?
ai.summary: This tradition, narrated by Imam Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him), extends the Prophet’s etiquette of privacy during defecation to include refraining from responding to others, thereby preserving mental focus and dignity. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the concept of *adab* (etiquette) as an integral part of worship, linking physical purity with spiritual mindfulness. The prohibition highlights that even simple social interactions should be suspended to maintain the sanctity of the bodily function.
